category_title: Students who demonstrate high engagement and responsiveness to visual schedules
student_description: This student is a highly energetic and expressive learner who frequently jumps up and down when excited but is easily derailed by visual distractions and crowded spaces. She does not naturally enjoy Adapted Physical Education (APE), meaning she requires a strong sense of autonomy and control to remain engaged. She thrives when teachers physically manage her visual field, embrace her high energy through rhythmic and physical joining, and provide choice-based visual schedules.

criteria.rationale: Since the student does not naturally enjoy APE, providing predictability and choice is critical for her to feel a sense of control and willingness to participate.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate a visual or picture schedule that allows the student to make choices about her upcoming activities.

criteria.rationale: Crowded or highly stimulating environments act as a trigger, requiring a proactive reduction in cognitive and instructional demands to prevent escalation.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include a strategy to lower instructional expectations and avoid introducing new skills when the environment is crowded or overstimulating.

criteria.rationale: On days when her behaviors escalate, pushing through the standard lesson plan will fail; she needs the environment adapted to prioritize her emotional regulation.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must explicitly allow for abandoning or completely changing the class structure to prioritize behavior management and de-escalation on difficult days.
